% Known-bad: item 1's ONLY figure values live in pic-quote angle labels
% ("$120^\circ$"/"$60^\circ$" — the skill's own taught circle-angles template,
% references/latex-templates.md). A detector that reads only \node text and
% macro args calls this list "no valued figures" and the mixed list passes —
% the false-PASS direction on the all-or-nothing figure-scope rule.
\documentclass{article}\usepackage{tikz,enumitem}\usetikzlibrary{angles,quotes}
\begin{document}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=3cm]
  \item Arc $PQ$ subtends the angles shown. Find the inscribed angle rule.
    \begin{center}
    \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9]
      \draw[thick] (0,0) circle (2);
      \coordinate (O) at (0,0);
      \coordinate (P) at (150:2);
      \coordinate (Q) at (30:2);
      \coordinate (R) at (270:2);
      \draw[thick] (P) -- (O) -- (Q);
      \draw[thick] (P) -- (R) -- (Q);
      \fill (O) circle (1.2pt);
      \node[below]      at (O) {$O$};
      \node[above left] at (P) {$P$};
      \node[above right] at (Q) {$Q$};
      \node[below]      at (R) {$R$};
      \pic [draw, angle radius=5mm, angle eccentricity=1.9, "$120^\circ$"] {angle = Q--O--P};
      \pic [draw, angle radius=7mm, angle eccentricity=1.6, "$60^\circ$"]  {angle = Q--R--P};
    \end{tikzpicture}
    \end{center}
  \item A central angle and its inscribed angle share an arc. State the ratio.
  \item An inscribed angle measures half its central angle. Explain why.
\end{enumerate}
\end{document}
